title: The AI review loop
purpose: See how a sandbox and approvals keep an AI agent's edits safe to merge.
sequence_reason: Prompt, proposed edit, sandbox, tests, review, and merge form a chronological loop, so motion shows the order better than one static diagram.
summary: You prompt the agent with context. It proposes an edit inside a workspace-write sandbox. Tests run in the same boundary, then you read the diff and merge only when it passes.
explanation: The sandbox sets technical boundaries and the approval policy decides when the agent must stop and ask.

learning_check.question: What does the sandbox boundary control, and what does the approval policy decide?
learning_check.answer: The sandbox controls which files the agent can edit and whether commands can use the network; the approval policy decides when the agent must stop and ask.

scenes.heading: The AI review loop
scenes.narration: An AI agent can edit your code. Watch the loop that keeps you in charge.

scenes.heading: One loop, six steps
scenes.narration: You prompt with context. The agent proposes an edit in the sandbox, tests run, you review the diff, then merge.

scenes.heading: Inside the sandbox vs beyond it
scenes.narration: Inside the sandbox the agent edits and runs tests without asking. To touch the network or other folders, it stops and asks.

path.label: Autonomous: no prompt inside the sandbox

scenes.heading: The review gate
scenes.narration: Before you merge, read the diff and check the tests. Merge only when both are good.

items: Merge only when both are good

scenes.heading: Why run the loop
scenes.narration: Skip the loop and the agent's mistake ships. Run the loop, and you catch it before it reaches your branch.

visual.verdict: Never merge AI output without review.
